newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Agriculture drives slowing S.African economy in Q2.
newsitem.headline: Agriculture drives slowing S.African economy in Q2.

text.p: A buoyant agricultural sector was the only highlight in an economy which showed signs of a significant slowdown in the second quarter of this year, economists said on Tuesday.

Latest Central Statistical Service data showed gross domestic product (GDP) grew at a seasonally adjusted and annualised rate of 3.5 percent in the second quarter compared with 3.3 percent in the first quarter of the year.
The agricultural sector, which has direct effect of about 4.5 percent on overall growth, weighed in with a 41.2 percent increase compared with a revised 80.1 percent rise in the first quarter.
Economists attributed the second quarter increase to the beginning of the harvesting of this year's bumper maize crop, which is put at a record 9.66 million tonnes.
Nedcor economist Kevin Lings noted, however, that the bulk of the harvesting had taken place in July and August, which would feed into the third quarter GDP data.
SMK Securities economist Herman van Papendorp said after stripping agriculture out of the overall figure, the latest statistics were evidence of a significant slowdown in the economy.
"On the non-primary side, if you include the mining sector (growth) is up 1.9 percent year-on-year in the second quarter from 5.2 percent in the second quarter of 1995," van Papendorp said.
A slowdown in gold output in the second quarter resulted in the mining sector showing negative growth of 1.0 percent from 0.6 percent growth in the first quarter.

Van Papendorp also said that the manufacturing sector, which contributes about 25 percent to GDP, had declined from a 9.9 percent year-on-year increase in the second quarter of 1995 to a negative 0.4 percent year-on-year in the latest quarter.
On a quarter-on-quarter basis, the sector grew 1.2 percent compared with negative growth of 0.7 percent in the first quarter.
He noted that the finance sector, which has a weighting of about 15.3 percent, also showed signs of easing although it was propped up by high private sector credit demand.
"There are signs of a downward trend in the finance sector, but it is not a major trend."
He said growth in the finance sector had eased to 3.1 percent year-on-year in the second quarter from 3.9 percent in the second quarter of 1995.
Economists said the latest data did little to alter their forecasts for growth of about three percent for the year.

Reserve Bank Governor Chris Stals also said earlier on Tuesday that South Africa was still set to achieve about 3.0 percent growth in 1996, noting that the main impetus would be provided by the recovery in the agricultural sector.
